faq.heading: Common Questions
faq.intro: Straight answers to what homeowners and facility managers ask us most. Don't see yours? Call or send the form and we'll walk you through it.

items.question: How long does a garage floor take?
items.answer: Most two- and three-car garages are ground, repaired, coated, and flaked in a single day. You can walk on the floor the next morning, move light items back in after 24 hours, and park on it after 48 hours. Larger shops and commercial floors are scheduled in phases so you can keep working.

items.question: What's the difference between epoxy and polyaspartic?
items.answer: Epoxy is a thick, strong base coat that bonds to the concrete and builds the floor. Polyaspartic is a faster-curing, UV-stable topcoat that won't yellow in sunlight and resists hot-tire pickup and chemicals. We use epoxy where it belongs, on the base, and polyaspartic on top, which is why our floors go in fast and hold up outdoors.

items.question: How do you prep the concrete?
items.answer: Every floor is diamond-ground with dust-collecting grinders to open the pores of the concrete so the coating bonds mechanically. We then fill cracks and spalls, grind them flush, check for moisture, and vacuum everything before the first coat goes down. Acid etching and paint rollers from a big-box kit skip this step, which is why those floors peel.

items.question: Will it peel or hot-tire lift like the kit I tried?
items.answer: No. Peeling comes from poor prep and thin, water-based coatings. We grind the slab, use 100% solids epoxy for the base, and finish with a polyaspartic topcoat that stays put under hot tires, dropped tools, and oil. Our residential floors carry a 15-year warranty against peeling and delamination.

items.question: Can you coat old, cracked, or stained concrete?
items.answer: Almost always. Cracks and chips are repaired and ground flush before coating, and a full-flake floor hides stains and surface imperfections completely. During the free estimate we test for moisture and check for structural problems; if a slab needs a moisture-mitigation primer or isn't a good candidate, we'll tell you up front.

items.question: Is it slippery when wet?
items.answer: A full-flake floor has natural texture from the chips, and we can add an anti-slip additive to the topcoat for patios, pool decks, entryways, and shop bays where water or oil is expected. Glossy marble floors can be finished satin or with a light grit for the same reason.

items.question: How do I clean and maintain it?
items.answer: Sweep or dust-mop as needed and hose it off or mop with warm water and a little neutral cleaner. There's no waxing or sealing to keep up with. Avoid rubber-backed mats sitting in one spot for months and use a dolly instead of dragging heavy steel edges across the floor.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: Pricing depends on square footage, the condition of the concrete, and the system you choose, so we quote every floor after a free on-site measurement. A typical two-car garage flake floor is priced by the square foot, and bigger shops and commercial floors get volume pricing. There's never a charge for the estimate.

items.question: Do you work on commercial and industrial floors?
items.answer: Yes. We install high-build epoxy, urethane mortar, and quartz systems for warehouses, shops, restaurant kitchens, gyms, clinics, and retail spaces, including line striping, safety zones, cove base, and drains. Night and weekend installs are available so you don't lose production time.

items.question: Are you licensed and insured?
items.answer: We're a veteran owned and operated company, fully insured, and every crew member on your property works directly for us. Ask and we'll gladly send a certificate of insurance before the job starts.

full-flake.title: Epoxy Flake Floors
full-flake.intro: Vinyl color chips broadcast into a 100% solids epoxy base and locked under a UV-stable polyaspartic topcoat. It's the floor we install more than any other, because it looks good on day one and still looks good ten years later.

sections.heading: Where Epoxy Flake Floors Can Be Used
body: Flake works anywhere concrete takes abuse and needs to stay clean. The texture hides dust and tire marks, and the topcoat shrugs off water, sun, and chemicals, so the same system covers a two-car garage, a covered patio, and a 10,000 sq ft shop.
bullets: Residential garages and carports
Workshops, barns, and metal buildings
Patios, porches, walkways, and pool decks
Basements, laundry rooms, and mudrooms
Auto shops, detail bays, and showrooms
Retail floors, gyms, vet clinics, and locker rooms
Warehouses, storage rooms, and light manufacturing

sections.heading: Why Choose Epoxy Flakes
body: A flake floor isn't paint. It's a bonded, seamless coating system that becomes part of the slab. Compared with bare concrete, tile, or a roll-on kit, it holds up better and costs less over its life.
bullets: Hot-tire resistant: the polyaspartic topcoat won't lift or peel under a warm tire
Hides dirt, dust, and stains between cleanings
UV stable, so outdoor and sun-facing floors don't yellow or chalk
Seals porous concrete against oil, salt, and moisture stains
Installed in one day on most garages, back in use within 48 hours
30+ color blends to match trim, cabinets, or brand colors
Backed by our 15-year residential warranty against peeling

sections.heading: The Installation Process
body: Every floor gets the same prep whether it's 400 square feet or 40,000. Most of the work, and most of the difference between a floor that lasts and one that peels, is in the first two steps.

steps.title: Estimate & moisture test
steps.text: We measure the space, check the slab for moisture and existing coatings, and pick a blend and finish with you.

steps.title: Diamond grinding
steps.text: Industrial grinders with dust extraction open the pores of the concrete so the epoxy bonds mechanically. No acid etching.

steps.title: Crack & spall repair
steps.text: Cracks, chips, and joints are filled with a fast-cure repair mortar and ground flush.

steps.title: Base coat
steps.text: A pigmented 100% solids epoxy or polyaspartic base coat is rolled on and back-rolled for even build.

steps.title: Flake broadcast
steps.text: Vinyl chips are broadcast into the wet base coat to full refusal, so no base color shows through.

steps.title: Scrape & vacuum
steps.text: Once cured, loose chips are scraped off and vacuumed, leaving a uniform, lightly textured surface.

steps.title: Clear topcoat
steps.text: A UV-stable polyaspartic clear coat locks the chips in and adds the gloss, chemical resistance, and optional anti-slip grit.

steps.title: Cure & walk-through
steps.text: Walk on it the next morning, move light items back after 24 hours, and park after 48. We walk the floor with you before we leave.

sections.heading: Safety Features
body: Flake floors are used in commercial kitchens, hospitals, and fire stations for a reason: they're easier to keep safe than the concrete they cover.
bullets: Built-in texture from the chips gives more grip than smooth concrete or tile
Optional anti-slip aggregate in the topcoat for wet areas, pool decks, and entries
Seamless surface with no grout lines, cracks, or edges to trip on
Light-colored blends brighten garages and shops and improve visibility
Chemical resistant, so spilled oil, gas, brake fluid, and cleaners wipe up instead of soaking in
Low-odor polyaspartic topcoats let you back in the space the same day
Cove base and drain detailing available where floors need to be washed down

sections.heading: Maintaining Your Epoxy Floor
body: There's no sealing, waxing, or refinishing schedule. A little routine care keeps a flake floor looking new for years.
bullets: Sweep or dust-mop as needed; rinse with a hose or mop with warm water and a neutral cleaner
Wipe up oil, gas, and chemical spills when you see them
Skip harsh solvents, citrus strippers, and abrasive pads
Put a pad under jack stands, kickstands, and sharp steel edges
Lift heavy equipment instead of dragging it across the floor
If a section ever dulls after years of hard use, a fresh clear coat brings it back without redoing the floor

solid-color.title: Solid Color Epoxy Floors
solid-color.intro: A single, uniform color of 100% solids epoxy rolled over a diamond-ground slab and sealed with a chemical-resistant urethane or polyaspartic topcoat. No chips, no pattern, just a smooth, bright, easy-to-clean surface that takes striping and logos well.
solid-color.ctaHeading: Ready for a cleaner, tougher floor?
solid-color.ctaText: Free on-site estimates across East Texas. Shops and commercial floors are scheduled around your hours.

sections.heading: Where Solid Color Floors Can Be Used
body: Solid color is the go-to system where the floor is a work surface first: places that get striped, hosed down, driven on by forklifts, or need to look clean and bright under fluorescent light. It's also the base for logos, color-coded zones, and safety markings.
bullets: Warehouses, distribution centers, and loading docks
Manufacturing floors and production lines
Auto repair bays, tire shops, and detail shops
Fire stations, fleet garages, and equipment barns
Commercial kitchens, breweries, and food prep areas
Retail back-of-house, stockrooms, and storage
Mechanical rooms, hallways, and stairwells
Home shops and garages that want a clean, simple look

sections.heading: Why Choose a Solid Color Floor
body: It's the most economical coating system we install, and in a working building it's often the most practical. A uniform color shows spills and dropped parts immediately, reflects light back into the space, and gives you a blank canvas for striping and branding.
bullets: Lowest cost per square foot of any coating system
Brightens the space: light gray and white floors bounce light and cut lighting costs
Easy to see leaks, spills, and dropped hardware
Seamless and non-porous, so oil, coolant, and chemicals wipe up instead of soaking in
Striping, safety zones, and logos bond directly into the system
Spot repairs and re-coats blend in without a visible patch
Available in 15 standard colors, or color-matched to a brand

sections.heading: The Installation Process
body: The prep is identical to our flake and metallic floors. The difference is in the build: a pigmented base, an optional second coat for extra thickness, and a clear protective topcoat.

steps.title: Estimate & moisture test
steps.text: We measure the space, check the slab for moisture, oil saturation, and old coatings, and pick a color and finish with you.

steps.title: Diamond grinding
steps.text: Industrial grinders with dust extraction profile the concrete so the epoxy bonds mechanically. No acid etching.

steps.title: Crack & joint repair
steps.text: Cracks, spalls, and control joints are filled with a fast-cure repair mortar and ground flush.

steps.title: Pigmented base coat
steps.text: A 100% solids epoxy in your color is rolled on and back-rolled for a uniform, even build.

steps.title: Second coat (optional)
steps.text: Heavy-traffic floors get a second pigmented coat, or a high-build epoxy, for extra thickness and impact resistance.

steps.title: Striping & markings
steps.text: Bay lines, aisles, safety zones, and logos are masked and applied before the topcoat so they're sealed in.

steps.title: Clear topcoat
steps.text: A chemical-resistant urethane or UV-stable polyaspartic clear coat adds the gloss, wear layer, and optional anti-slip grit.

steps.title: Cure & turnover
steps.text: Foot traffic the next morning, rolling loads after 48 hours, full chemical resistance within a week. We schedule nights and weekends to keep you running.

sections.heading: Safety Features
body: A solid color floor is the standard in facilities where safety is audited, because everything about it can be seen, marked, and cleaned.
bullets: Anti-slip aggregate available in the topcoat for wet areas, wash bays, and ramps
High-visibility striping for forklift aisles, pedestrian walkways, and keep-clear zones
Light colors improve visibility and make hazards and spills obvious
Seamless surface with no joints, cracks, or edges to trip on or trap bacteria
Chemical and fuel resistant, so spills stay on top where they can be cleaned
Cove base and drain detailing where floors need to be washed down
USDA/FDA-compliant systems for food and beverage spaces

sections.heading: Maintaining Your Solid Color Floor
body: No waxing, sealing, or buffing. Routine cleaning and a little common sense keep a solid color floor looking new, and it's the easiest system to touch up when a shop earns its scars.
bullets: Sweep or dust-mop daily in working spaces; auto-scrub or mop with a neutral cleaner as needed
Wipe up oil, coolant, brake fluid, and solvents when you see them
Avoid dragging steel edges or dropping heavy tools; use pads under jack stands and equipment feet
Skip harsh strippers and abrasive pads that dull the topcoat
Use non-marking tires on forklifts and carts where possible
A fresh clear coat every several years, or in the high-wear lanes only, brings the floor back without redoing it

metallic-marble.title: Metallic & Marble Epoxy Floors
metallic-marble.intro: Metallic pearl pigments are blended into clear 100% solids epoxy and hand-worked across the floor so the pigment drifts, pools, and veins as it cures. The result looks like polished marble, lava, or brushed metal, and no two floors are ever alike.
metallic-marble.ctaHeading: Want a floor nobody else has?
metallic-marble.ctaText: Free on-site estimates across East Texas. Bring a color idea or a photo you like and we'll match a pour to it.

sections.heading: Where Metallic & Marble Floors Can Be Used
body: Metallic floors go where the floor is meant to be seen. They're most often chosen for finished living space and for businesses that want the floor to be part of the brand. Indoors is the rule: the epoxy base isn't UV stable, so for a covered patio or sun room we build the same look with a UV-stable topcoat.
bullets: Finished basements, game rooms, and home theaters
Living rooms, kitchens, and open-plan remodels on slab
Show garages and car collections
Barbershops, salons, tattoo studios, and boutiques
Restaurants, bars, breweries, and coffee shops
Showrooms, lobbies, and office reception areas
Gyms, studios, and clinics that want a premium look
Retail floors and event spaces

sections.heading: Why Choose a Metallic & Marble Floor
body: It's the closest thing to polished stone you can put over an existing slab, at a fraction of the cost of real marble or terrazzo, with none of the grout lines and a fraction of the maintenance.
bullets: Truly one of a kind: the pigment moves as it cures, so your floor's pattern exists nowhere else
Depth and shine that changes with the light and the angle you view it from
Two- and three-color pours, from subtle silver and charcoal to bold copper, blue, or red
Seamless surface with no grout lines to stain or crack
Far less expensive than natural stone, terrazzo, or large-format tile
Same tough epoxy and urethane build as our commercial floors underneath
Covers stained, ugly, or previously coated concrete completely

sections.heading: The Installation Process
body: Prep is the same as every floor we install. The difference is the pour itself: metallic floors are built up in coats and worked by hand while wet, so timing and technique matter more than with any other system.

steps.title: Design & estimate
steps.text: We look at the space and the light, pick your base and accent pigments, and decide on the technique: veined, dropped, or full-swirl marble.

steps.title: Diamond grinding
steps.text: Dust-free grinders open the concrete so the epoxy bonds. Old coatings, adhesives, and paint are removed completely.

steps.title: Crack & surface repair
steps.text: Cracks, joints, and pits are filled and ground flush. Metallic floors are glossy, so surface prep is especially thorough.

steps.title: Pigmented base coat
steps.text: A solid-color epoxy base, usually black or charcoal, is applied so the metallic layer has a dark background to play against.

steps.title: Metallic pour
steps.text: Clear epoxy loaded with pearl pigment is poured and spread, then a second color is dropped in and worked with rollers, brushes, and a light mist of solvent to move the pigment into veins and cells.

steps.title: Cure
steps.text: The floor is left untouched, in a closed room, while the pattern settles and hardens. Dust and foot traffic are kept out for a full day.

steps.title: Clear topcoat
steps.text: A high-gloss or satin urethane clear coat locks in the pattern and provides the scratch, chemical, and UV protection.

steps.title: Walk-through
steps.text: Walk on it after 24 hours and move furniture back after 72. We walk the floor with you and go over care before we leave.

sections.heading: Safety Features
body: A metallic floor is a glossy floor, so we plan for grip up front and build the rest of the safety in the same way we do for commercial work.
bullets: Anti-slip additive available in the topcoat for entries, kitchens, and salons where floors get wet
Satin finish option that keeps the depth while cutting glare and slickness
Seamless surface with no grout lines, edges, or transitions to trip on
Non-porous and easy to sanitize, which is why salons, studios, and clinics choose it
Chemical, stain, and abrasion resistant urethane topcoat
Low-odor materials and a sealed cure room; you're back in the space within a day or two
Cove base and threshold detailing available for wet rooms

sections.heading: Maintaining Your Metallic Floor
body: There's no polishing, waxing, or resealing on a schedule. Keep grit off it, clean spills, and it stays glassy for years.
bullets: Dust-mop or vacuum with a soft head regularly; grit is what dulls a glossy floor
Damp-mop with warm water and a pH-neutral cleaner; skip vinegar, bleach, and abrasive powders
Wipe up spills, especially hair dye, wine, and oil, when you see them
Use felt pads under furniture and mats at exterior doors
Avoid dragging appliances or steel edges across the surface
If the gloss ever dulls in a traffic lane after years of use, a fresh clear coat restores the shine without touching the pattern
